subjects.label: The Alien as an opponent
subjects.description: The xenomorph itself as an adversary: how its AI hunts rather than follows a script, how acute its senses are, how it learns and adapts to your tricks, and that it cannot be killed or reliably shaken off; not the fear it produces and not the station's other enemies.

subjects.label: Hiding, lockers and crouching
subjects.description: The player's side of the hunt: lockers and cabinets, crouching under desks, vents, staying still and being unable to run, and the hide-and-seek rhythm the whole game is played in; not the Alien's own behaviour and not the controls as such.

subjects.label: Saving at terminals
subjects.description: The save system specifically: being able to save only at fixed emergency terminals, the dread of dying before reaching one, and whether losing a long stretch of progress is the tension the game wants or simply punishment; not general difficulty or checkpoint placement in combat.

subjects.label: The android enemies
subjects.description: The synthetic humans as a second, separate threat: how they look, move and bleed, players who find them worse than the Alien, and the long android-heavy stretches of the game; not the Alien and not the human survivors.
